entities.summary: The Terrorist Financing Convention is a 1999 United Nations treaty designed to criminalize acts of financing acts of terrorism. The convention also seeks to promote police and judicial co-operation to prevent, investigate and punish the financing of such acts. The Convention was negotiated following the 1996 UNGA Resolution 51/210 and a G-8 counter-terrorism initiative, and adopted by consensus by the UN General Assembly as Resolution 54/109 on 9 December 1999 at its fourth session. As of October 2018, the treaty has been ratified by 188 states; in terms of universality, it is therefore one of the most successful anti-terrorism treaties in history.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The International Convention for the Suppression of the Financing of Terrorism has had a significant impact on global counter-terrorism efforts, with 188 states having ratified it as of October 2018. This treaty has promoted police and judicial cooperation to prevent, investigate, and punish financing of terrorism, contributing to a safer world.
